caption: The drawing features a single, large, cylindrical stoneware jug or crock, rendered in shades of brown with a slightly darker brown color used to indicate shadows and the depth of the vessel's interior. The jug has a pair of small, protruding handles near the top on each side, and a slightly flared rim. On the front surface of the jug, there is a decorative blue design consisting of five stylized, curved leaves arranged in an upward and outward pattern. Beneath this design, the numbers “1856” are inscribed in blue, possibly indicating a year. Below the numbers is a blue squiggle. At the bottom of the drawing, outside the jug, the number “5” is written in blue, followed by the name “W. DUNN” in uppercase blue letters. In the bottom right-hand corner, there appears to be a faint signature, “RICHARD B...”, with the rest partially cut off or faded. The background is plain and uncolored, giving the whole composition a simple, centered layout.
title: Five Gallon Churn
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
